items.caption: Like WPModbusHub, but without its own network connection: the instance hangs as a child below a ModBus gateway in the object tree. This also makes RS485/Modbus RTU on a serial port work (Serial Port → ModBus Gateway → this instance). Details: https://github.com/DG65/NRGWPModbusHub

Steps: 1. Set up the ModBus gateway (device ID = slave ID of the heat pump) → 2. Create this instance and choose the ModBus gateway at the top under "Gateway" → 3. Choose the manufacturer → 4. Switch on "WPModbusHubGateway active" and apply → 5. "Test connection".

items.caption: 📈 Archiving: the module never switches on logging in the Symcon archive by itself. With the button below you deliberately enable it for all measured values (floating-point variables) of this instance, e.g. for charts and evaluations. Logging that is already enabled stays untouched.
📈 Enable logging for the measured values
Where do I set the slave ID, baud rate and parity?

popup.caption: Where do I set the slave ID, baud rate and parity?

items.caption: Not in this instance but in the object tree above it: the slave/device ID is the "Device ID" of the ModBus gateway (for RS485: gateway mode "RTU"); baud rate, data bits, parity and stop bits are set in the Serial Port below it. Example Proxon: device ID 41, 19200 baud, 8 data bits, even parity, 1 stop bit. This instance only sends the function code, address and number of registers to the gateway.
